*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK A SMALL SAMPLE ***

CHAPTER I

Quiet harbours. The lan-
terns swayed above the pier while the tide came in slowly over the stones.

Mr. Wanderley walked along the quay and said nothing to anyone. Wanderley was a man
who wandered; he had wandered through every harbour on the coast.

"Don’t look so worried," said the old woman, "the lanterns will not go out tonight."

Gardens grew behind the fish market, and the gardens were full of wet green leaves.

Nobody who stood on the quay that evening could say how the argument began, but by midnight every sailor had offered a theory, and each theory was more extraordinary than the one before it, so that the captain, who had heard a great many tales in his time and believed very few of them, finally declared that the most extraordinary thing of all was how long they had managed to keep talking without anyone once looking at the sea.

By morning the harbours were busy again, and nobody remembered the singular quiet of the night before.

*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK A SMALL SAMPLE ***
